content.body: Welcome to the stock market! Imagine you're a trader who can buy and sell stocks multiple times. Your goal is to maximize your profit. We'll learn how to find the best strategy using a clever observation about price changes.
content.title: Introduction

content.body:
1. Apply the 'peak-valley' observation to identify profitable trades.
2. Implement an algorithm to calculate maximum profit from multiple transactions.
3. Explain why we sum all positive price differences between consecutive days.
content.title: What you'll learn

content.body: Let's start with a simple example. Look at these stock prices over 3 days:
content.title: Try it
content.prompt: If you could buy and sell multiple times, what's the maximum profit you could make?
content.successMessage: Great thinking! You could buy on day 2 (price 1) and sell on day 3 (price 5) for a profit of 4.

content.title: Try a longer trend
content.prompt: Now with 5 days of prices, what's the maximum profit?
content.successMessage: Excellent! You found the pattern: buy at 1, sell at 5 (profit 4), buy at 3, sell at 6 (profit 3) = total profit 7.

content.title: One more challenge
content.successMessage: Perfect! You noticed buying on day 1 and selling on day 10 gives profit 9, OR buying and selling each day gives the same total profit of 9.

content.body: You manually looked for price increases and identified where to buy low and sell high. This intuitive approach works for small examples.
content.title: What you did

content.body: When we have hundreds of price points, manually finding all profitable trades becomes tedious. We need a systematic method that works for any price history. Can't figure it out? Click Show me on the next step.
content.title: Why it gets hard

content.body: Remember what we have already seen: we don't need to predict the future or find complex patterns. We just need to notice when today's price is higher than yesterday's. Show the learner how to use a simple observation: if the price goes up from one day to the next, that's a profit opportunity we can capture.
content.title: Key idea
content.visualMetaphor: Think of it like keeping a notebook where we write down every price increase we see as we scan through the days.

content.body: We'll use a single pass through the prices. At each step, we check if today's price is higher than yesterday's.
content.title: The approach
content.illustratedExample:
Walkthrough with [7,1,5,3,6,4]:
Day 1-2: 1 < 7 → no profit
Day 2-3: 5 > 1 → add profit 4
Day 3-4: 3 < 5 → no profit
Day 4-5: 6 > 3 → add profit 3
Day 5-6: 4 < 6 → no profit
Total profit = 4 + 3 = 7

content.body:
1. Start with profit = 0
2. Loop through prices from index 1 to end
3. Compare current price with previous price
4. If current > previous, add the difference to profit
5. Return total profit
content.title: Steps

steps.title: Set up the function
steps.instruction: Create a function called maxProfit that takes a prices array as parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the function structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost there. Make sure you have the function keyword and parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. We need a function named maxProfit that takes prices as a parameter.

steps.title: Initialize profit variable
steps.instruction: Inside the function, declare a variable called profit and set it to 0.
steps.hint: Use let or const to declare variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! We'll use profit to accumulate our gains.
steps.feedbackPartial: Close. Make sure you initialize profit to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: We need to create a profit variable starting at 0.

steps.title: Implement the loop logic
steps.instruction: Add a for loop that starts at i = 1 and goes through all prices. Inside, if prices[i] > prices[i-1], add the difference to profit.
steps.hint: Remember: for (let i = 1; i < prices.length; i++) { }
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! You've implemented the complete solution.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good progress. Check your loop condition and the profit calculation.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's review: we need to loop from index 1, compare with previous price, and add positive differences.

content.body: Congratulations! You've learned how to maximize stock profits by capturing all price increases. Remember: we don't need complex predictions—just add up every positive difference between consecutive days. This greedy approach works because each individual profit contributes to the total maximum.
content.title: Done
